name_note: The GTDB name Mediterraneibacter gnavus corresponds to the classical Ruminococcus gnavus, reclassified into the genus Mediterraneibacter.

sentences.text: Mediterraneibacter gnavus, also called Ruminococcus gnavus, is a Gram-positive anaerobic bacterium of the human gut microbiota.
The species was formally transferred to Mediterraneibacter as M. gnavus comb. nov., with type strain ATCC 29149.

One report describes the bacterium as playing dual roles in health and disease, supporting nutrient metabolism essential for bodily functions while also contributing to the development of inflammatory bowel disease.
A study of fecal samples from NASH patients and controls reported enrichment of ethanol-producing bacteria including M. gnavus.
In a gut microbiome study of hypertension patients, Mediterraneibacter gnavus was reported to act as a key node in co-occurrence network analysis.
